subject: Urgent: SparkBridge SDK integration causing elevated latency and 502s — exec review
messages:
From: Sara Ong <sara.ong@sparkbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 17:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Production: Checkout latency + 502 spike (SparkBridge)

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 502s and p99 token latency from our Checkout integration at ~16:45 UTC. Errors correlate with bursts of long requests (user carts > 500 tokens) that use your client-side SDK to stream prompts. We've attached a sample of failing request traces and a set of raw request/response bytes (sparkbridge_sample_requests_1126.txt).

Impact: ~8% increase in error rate on checkout endpoints, p99 latency up from 320ms to 1.8s for token streaming, and several customer checkout timeouts. This is causing conversion drops for our peak traffic.

Initial notes from our side:
- Errors look like 502 Bad Gateway coming back from your hosted endpoint, not our frontend.
- When we disable streaming (fall back to non-streamed poll), traffic normalizes.
- We re-ran a small dev repro and saw the client drop a chunk mid-stream leading to a parser failure on the server.

Can you confirm if you're seeing similar traces and whether this maps to any recent SDK or runtime change? We need an ETA and whether we should plan a rollback/canary.

Thanks,
Sara
VP Engineering, SparkBridge

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 18:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Production: Checkout latency + 502 spike (SparkBridge)

Marissa / Rishi — dug into the ingress traces matching the IDs from Sara's attachment. Quick technical summary:

What we see:
- A subset of streaming requests contain an extra small trailer segment that the current client SDK emits when a 'final-meta' header is present.
- Our server-side streaming parser expects header frames to arrive in a single header preface and treats unexpected trailer-like frames as a separator; when a trailer chunk arrives mid-body it triggers a parser state reset. That reset leads to a dropped continuation token and a subsequent internal codec error, which surfaces upstream as a 502.
- In many cases the codec error is transient, but it introduces retries and head-of-line blocking that push p99 token latency up for other concurrent requests on the same worker.

Repro steps (local):
1) Client: enable chunked streaming with 'chunk-continue' and append an empty trailer for calls with metadata.
2) Server: current parser uses stateful header assembly that treats any frame with 'meta:' prefix as a header boundary.
3) Result: mid-stream trailer is misinterpreted and causes state machine to discard the current KV cache slice.

Root cause hypothesis: backwards-incompatible change in the SDK's chunk framing plus our parser's aggressive boundary detection.

Short-term mitigation we can roll in ~2 hours:
- Deploy a parser tolerant mode (INF-8421) that treats 'final-meta' trailers as inline metadata (non-boundary). This is a config flip we can canary for SparkBridge only.
- If tolerated mode isn't stable, we can push a quick client-side recommendation to disable 'chunk-continue' for SparkBridge until we ship a formal fix.

Longer term: we need a test harness pairing SDK chunk permutations with runtime parser modes and add these to CI.

I'll open the Jira INF-8421 with the trace snippets. ETA for the tolerant-mode canary: 90-120 minutes if infra cooperates.

—Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Exec brief: SparkBridge streaming failures — impact, root cause, mitigation plan

Team — sending the executive summary I promised. TL;DR: Integration between SparkBridge's client SDK (chunked streaming + 'final-meta' trailers) and our server parser produced a parser state reset on ~6% of streamed requests during peak, generating 502s and elevated p99 latency. Ben has a near-term tolerant-mode we can canary for SparkBridge alone.

Impact:
- Customer: checkout conversions affected, persistent errors during peak windows, customer flagged as at-risk for renewal (deal DB-12478).
- Scope: ~6-10% of streaming requests for SparkBridge during the 16:45–17:15 UTC spike window; aggregate p99 token latency rose to ~1.8s.
- Business: SparkBridge escalated to VP Eng (Sara Ong) and requested a remediation ETA and credit.

Root cause:
- SDK emitted a small trailer frame mid-stream when a 'final-meta' header was present. Our parser treated that trailer as a header boundary, forcing state machine reset and dropping continuation bytes. The drop produced a codec error -> 502 responses and retries that worsened head-of-line latency.

Mitigation plan:
- Immediate (canary in 1.5–2h): flip 'parser.tolerant_final_meta' for SparkBridge to true (INF-8421). This accepts inline trailers without resetting the parser boundary.
- Short (same day): advise SparkBridge to temporarily disable 'chunk-continue' on their SDK for affected endpoints while we validate canary.
- Medium (1 week): release runtime patch and coordinate with SDK team to add a flag that preserves old semantics and update CI to include combo tests.

Customer comms/team asks:
- Sales/Account: Marissa to prepare a customer-facing status update and propose a service credit. Lauren — can you draft the credit language for review by EOD?
- Exec decision: Do we approve a one-off service credit up to 5% of last-month invoice for SparkBridge pending final RCA?
- Infra: Ben/Rishi — please confirm canary readiness and rollback steps; include runbook.

I'll host a 09:30 PT sync if needed; otherwise I'll send an updated status at 10:30 PT post-canary.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
